source_snapshot.html: A forecast origin is the record at which the report is issued. Mature training outcomes are completed future-path labels available by the latest scheduled refit. Fixed-at-refit (frozen) F holds that label pool between refits; per-origin (rolling) F refreshes it at each forecast origin. Both update the observed current anchor. Historical peaks use their original recorded positions; translated increments shift historical signed paths to the current position. Headroom is the nonnegative excess above the observed floor, the absolute current position. These are forecasting definitions, not cash-resource allocations.

All fitted methods use mature training outcomes; controls distinguish per-origin and fixed-at-refit updates.

source_snapshot.html: Let N denote the signed source-reported net position. The issue magnitude B is observed when the report is issued. Define the sampled peak P and its nonnegative headroom G by
B<sub>t</sub>=|N<sub>t</sub>|;   P<sub>t,H</sub>=max<sub>0≤h≤H</sub>|N<sub>t+h</sub>|;   G<sub>t,H</sub>=P<sub>t,H</sub>−B<sub>t</sub>≥0.
At issue t, the most recent scheduled refit is κ(t). Every training label is complete by that refit, and the next refit updates the transform, scale, coefficients and historical pool together:
κ(t)=t<sub>0</sub>+d ⌊(t−t<sub>0</sub>)/d⌋;   T<sub>κ,H,W</sub>={κ−H−W+1,...,κ−H}.

For a completed episode i, let u and l be its largest and smallest increments from its starting position, including the zero increment. Translating its ordered path to x=N<sub>t</sub> produces V<sub>i,t</sub>=max{x+u<sub>i</sub>,−x−l<sub>i</sub>}. On a common episode set A, Q selects the duplicate-preserving corrected empirical order statistic. The historical forecasts are

C<sub>t</sub><super>F</super>=B<sub>t</sub>+Q{G<sub>i,H</sub>:i∈A};   C<sub>t</sub><super>S</super>=B<sub>t</sub>+Q{V<sub>i,t</sub>−B<sub>t</sub>:i∈A};   C<sub>t</sub><super>K</super>=max{B<sub>t</sub>,Q{P<sub>i,H</sub>:i∈A}}.

Rolling controls update their completed-label set at each issue. Frozen controls use the same mature training-outcome pool and refit schedule as the fitted procedures, while their current issue anchor continues to update. Earlier one-state controls retrieve nearby signed starting positions; their complete earlier menus remain in Supplement S3.

The 33 raw coordinates are N(t) through N(t−24), current magnitude, short/long past increment root-mean-square (RMS) summaries, sine/cosine of recorded hour, sine/cosine of weekday (Monday zero), and whether the just-observed adjacent gap exceeds its nominal interval. RMS spans are 24/168 FX records and 6/26 Treasury records; nominal gaps are 3600 and 604800 seconds. Calendar coordinates follow the stored source clock; constant training columns are centered exactly at their repeated value.

v<sub>L</sub>(t)=[L<super>−1</super> ∑<sub>j=t−L+1</sub><super>t</super>(N<sub>j</sub>−N<sub>j−1</sub>)<super>2</super>]<super>1/2</super>;   z<sub>i,κ,j</sub>=(x<sub>ij</sub>−μ<sub>κj</sub>)/s<sub>κj</sub>.

Training-only centering and population standard deviations define z. An exactly constant coordinate receives unit scale after centering. Matching completed response origins retains the different past-only lookbacks required by the feature construction. The response scale a is computed from completed training headrooms and magnitudes:
a<sub>κ</sub>=max{mean<sub>i ∈ T</sub>(G<sub>i,H</sub>),10<super>−6</super> mean<sub>i ∈ T</sub>|N<sub>i</sub>|,10<super>−12</super>}.

QR minimizes the normalized headroom regression-quantile objective with an unpenalized intercept and a ridge penalty on slopes. The fixed menu is λ in {0.001,0.01,0.1}; τ=19/20. Training uses the unconstrained affine headroom prediction. Nonnegative projection is applied when issuing and validating a report, rather than inside the training objective; validation uses native units.
min<sub>β<sub>0</sub>,β</sub> W<super>−1</super> ∑<sub>i ∈ T</sub> ρ<sub>τ</sub>(G<sub>i,H</sub>/a<sub>κ</sub>−β<sub>0</sub>−z<sub>i,κ</sub><super>T</super>β)+(λ/2)‖β‖<sub>2</sub><super>2</super>.
C<sub>t</sub><super>QR</super>=B<sub>t</sub>+max{0,a<sub>κ</sub>(β̂<sub>0,κ</sub>+z<sub>t,κ</sub><super>T</super>β̂<sub>κ</sub>)}.

The intercept is unpenalized and slopes receive a ridge penalty. Adding B to a headroom quantile translates it into a peak quantile; projecting a report up to the known response floor weakly improves realized pinball loss. The equivalent peak parameterization and numerical conventions are retained in Supplement S4.

KNN uses training-standardized features with the frozen group weights and recency tie-breaking rule specified in Supplement S4. It reports B plus a local headroom quantile. Scaled KNN divides each selected headroom by its past short RMS and multiplies the resulting quantile by the query RMS, using the same fixed stabilizer within each refit block.

s<sub>i|κ</sub>=max{v<sub>short</sub>(i),10<super>−6</super>a<sub>κ</sub>};   C<sub>t</sub><super>scaled</super>=B<sub>t</sub>+s<sub>t|κ</sub>Q<sub>k</sub>({G<sub>i,H</sub>/s<sub>i|κ</sub>:i∈N<sub>t,κ,k</sub>}).

The neighbor menus are {180,360,720} at both FX windows, {20,40,52} at Treasury W52, and {40,80,160} at W260. The implementation uses exact order statistics and fails on an unavailable rank. For k=52, ⌈(k+1).95⌉=51, while the ordinary .95 empirical pinball quantile has rank 50. At W720, W2880 and W260, however, W times .95 is integer: the lower ordinary rank and the adjacent corrected rank are both endpoints of the empirical pinball minimizer interval. The W52 distinction is specific to its noninteger probability-times-pool-size case. A later endpoint/rank ablation is retained in Supplement S5. Plain KNN at k=W equals frozen F exactly; membership is then the complete training pool. Scaled KNN still changes responses at k=W. Long-window menus restrict neighborhood sizes below the full pool. Supplement S4 records numerical acceptance and failures.

source_snapshot.text: Proposition 1. Known-floor projection and strict coverage

source_snapshot.html: Let the forecast-origin information include B, let Y≥B almost surely, and let 0<τ<1. Project any issued report c to max(B,c). Its pinball loss is no larger at every possible Y. A true conditional lower inverse quantile q at level τ=1−α has strict breach probability at most α. Equality is not automatic: an atom at the quantile can make the probability smaller. The lower bound alone need not create an outcome atom; fitted reports do not inherit the population statement.
ρ<sub>τ</sub>(Y−c)−ρ<sub>τ</sub>(Y−max(B,c))=τ(B−c)<sub>+</sub>;   Pr(Y>q | ℱ<sub>t</sub>)≤α.

Proof. Below B both errors are nonnegative, so their loss difference is the displayed nonnegative quantity; otherwise the report is unchanged. For the conditional inverse quantile, F(q)≥τ, hence the strict-tail probability is at most α. An atom is a possible reason for strict inequality, not a necessary premise. Accordingly, the retained equality-based coverage tests are diagnostics of their stated nulls, not automatic tests of every valid upper quantile.

Let future real increments be independent and individually symmetric about zero. Write S<sub>h</sub> for their partial sums, S<sub>0</sub>=0, and fix an observed starting position x with B=|x|. No identical-distribution or finite-moment assumption is required. If q is the population (1−α/2) quantile of |S<sub>H</sub>|, the report B+q has strict peak-breach probability at most α. This is a direct scalar application of the classical Lévy maximal inequality (Sussman, 2023), not a new inequality.
Pr(max<sub>0≤h≤H</sub>|x+S<sub>h</sub>|>B+q)≤Pr(max<sub>h</sub>|S<sub>h</sub>|>q)≤2Pr(|S<sub>H</sub>|>q)≤α.

Proof. The triangle inequality gives the first inclusion; Lévy’s maximal inequality and the inverse-quantile tail bound give the rest. For conditional coverage, independence and symmetry must hold conditional on origin information and q must be the corresponding conditional population quantile. The empirical plug-in L, overlapping historical labels and dependent mean-reverting data do not acquire that guarantee. A generic one-sided endpoint VaR is not the required absolute-displacement quantile. Supplement S15 gives an exact finite counterexample to that substitution; Supplement S11 retains the proof, original simulations and corrected sensitivities.

Use one nonempty historical pool, one available order-statistic rank k, and peaks that include their starting observation. Let F add historical peak headroom to the current B, S translate each historical signed path to x, and K floor the historical-peak order statistic at B. Their differences obey the following deterministic bounds. The common pool and same rank are essential; these are neither forecast-accuracy nor coverage guarantees.
|F−K|≤r<sub>abs</sub>=max<sub>i</sub>||N<sub>i</sub>|−B|;   |S−K|≤r<sub>signed</sub>=max<sub>i</sub>|N<sub>i</sub>−x|.

Proof. For each historical row, compare the headroom construction and translated path maximum to max(B,P<sub>i</sub>). Projection and the reverse triangle inequality bound their differences by the two anchor distances. A fixed order statistic is nonexpansive for the maximum paired difference, and flooring commutes with that order statistic. Applying these facts yields the displayed bounds. Supplement S2 retains the rowwise derivation and examples where the same observed history permits opposite loss rankings.

The operational report L uses the same frozen completed-origin pool and refit times as F. Its endpoint sample is |N<sub>i+H</sub>−N<sub>i</sub>| and its one-based order rank is ⌈39(W+1)/40⌉. Add the resulting estimate to B<sub>t</sub>. This empirical plug-in is distinct from the known population quantile in Proposition 2. Overlapping endpoint samples and dependent, changing series do not inherit the proposition’s population coverage. Conditional coverage additionally requires the independence and symmetry premises and the correct endpoint quantile conditional on issue information. The bound supplies no pinball-loss ordering against F.

Observed targets satisfy P(H6)≤P(H24), and population conditional quantiles under the same origin information inherit that ordering. Independently estimated forecasts need not: FX QR W720 crosses on 640/6625 issues (Supplement Table S15). A raise-only repair of the longer-horizon report can increase pinball loss, as the exact counterexample in Supplement S15 shows. This does not rule out all monotone rearrangements: with equally weighted ordered outcomes and a common quantile level, sorting can weakly reduce total pinball loss without guaranteeing each horizon improves. Crossing is a coherence diagnostic, not sufficient proof of calibration failure.

The historical controls also use current information: the headroom and floored-peak rules incorporate the observed magnitude, and path translation uses the current signed anchor. Conditional estimation is therefore compared with already anchored historical forecasts, not with a rule that ignores the current observation.

P(H6)≤P(H24); population conditional quantiles share this ordering only under the same origin information.
